title: Rapid hire instincts and scoring — Lucas Moreno loop
content:
Quick top-line: Lucas Moreno feels like a high-energy IC with strong systems instincts but has a few gaps around LLM-specific performance tradeoffs. Good culture fit, communicates clearly, and can own a subcomponent end-to-end after a short ramp. Not an immediate Sr-runtime architect but strong candidate for Senior Engineer on serving-runtime team with mentoring.

Session notes (raw):
- Round 1 (systems design, 45m): asked for high-level design of a multi-tenant GPU serving layer that supports model variants and safe rollbacks. Proposed a routing layer + lightweight per-customer config. Emphasized observability (per-route metrics) and canary toggles.
  - Likes: clear separation of control plane vs data plane, proposed using consistent hashing for model shard routing which simplifies locality.
  - Concerns: suggested ``sticky`` routing to avoid KV cache fragmentation but under-emphasized fallback load-shedding and preemptive cache warming. Needs prompting to consider token-level cache reuse.

- Round 2 (perf debugging, 40m): walked through CPU/GPU bottleneck scenarios; described a pipeline for async batching and priority queues. Gave good explanation of memory fragmentation on CUDA and proposed a compaction strategy.
  - Likes: concrete mitigation steps (pinned memory pools, eviction heuristics) and diagnostics to detect KV cache stalls.
  - Gaps: not familiar with recent quantized attention kernels (QK-transform tricks) and tradeoffs for int8 perf vs quality. Could learn quickly but will need pair time with infra or applied-ml.

- Round 3 (behaviors + collaboration, 30m): described prior work launching an internal staging cluster; emphasized clear runbooks and blameless postmortems. Had examples of mentoring new grads and shipping small infra features end-to-end.

Hand-scored heuristics (my ad-hoc scale 1-5):
- System design / architecture: 4
- Inference-specific low-level knowledge (quantization, kernels): 3
- Debugging / perf triage: 4
- Production judgement (SLOs, rollouts): 4
- Communication & collaboration: 5
- Ramp time to full ownership of a serving subcomponent: ~6-8 weeks estimate

Red flags / unresolved questions to follow up:
- Wants to drive model-level profiling but has more exposure to infra-level perf (network, CUDA). Check concrete experience with KV-cache-aware batching and memory reuse patterns.
- Not tested on heavy-scale routing policies: need a short take-home or practical scenario: design routing policy for mixed-tenancy with bursty tails (include cost-awareness + SLA) — Lucas seemed to have good instincts but would benefit from problem constraints in writing.

Hiring recommendation (quick): strong hire for Senior Engineer (serving runtime) with training plan: pair with Diego Ramos or Applied-ML for 2–4 weeks on quantization/kernel tradeoffs; 1-month rotation on canary/rollout story with Marcus. Not yet a clear match for Sr Runtime Architect (wider cross-org ownership) until quant/kernels depth proven.

Suggested feedback bullets for panel:
- "Clear communicator, strong systems fundamentals; will accelerate operational reliability work and own medium-sized runtime features end-to-end."
- "Needs brushing up on latest quantization kernels and model-level caching patterns — recommend pairing with applied-ml initially."
- "High collaboration signal and mentoring experience; immediate positive culture add."

Notes to self (things to record in candidate thread):
- Ask Lucas for two specific perf diffs he's owned (before/after metrics), plus the PRs or dashboard links. Capture the PR where he designed the eviction heuristic.
- Follow up with a 1-week paid mini-project: small puzzle to design prefix-KV caching for a prompt-heavy product (timebox 3–4 hours) — use this to validate cache reasoning.

Draft snippet for hiring doc (short):
- "Lucas demonstrated strong systems thinking and production traction. Recommend hire at Senior Engineer on serving-runtime. Provide onboarding plan focused on quantization and model-aware caching. Manager: TBD; pair first quarter with Applied-ML & SRE."

Random scratch items:
- Jira I left open in interview: RED-1421 (canary fallout postmortem template) — mention as interview talking point.
- Possible ref check: ex-manager "Talia Morgan" at previous company (note: she reported test infra deliverable timeline accuracy).

Immediate next steps:
1) Add my quick scores to the candidate thread and vote.
2) Ping Priya for final calibration with hiring bar rubric (ask for threshold on quant expertise).
3) Email Lucas with mini-project if we want to validate cache reasoning before offer.

Unpolished thoughts / heuristics for future loops (note to self):
- Prefer candidates who can articulate both high-level SLO choices and 3 concrete debugging steps for tail latency. If they can only do one consistently, that leans toward IC+ but not architect.
- Practical signal: a PR that includes both metric dashboards + the rollout config change (shows ownership across design->obs->ops).

End of notes.
